annotation.authors_or_issuer: Niemelä, M.; van Aerschot, L.; Tammela, A.; Aaltonen, I.; Lammi, H.
key_provisions_or_claims: Telepresence robots increase family presence and possibly engagement in residential care.
Privacy is the central concern, especially with robot mobility in wards.
Mobility of telepresence robots is hard to use in care settings without ethical guidelines.
Care workers' perspective and acceptance are critical; the robot may add workload.
The paper proposes a draft of ethical guidelines for telepresence robot use in residential care.
annotation.summary_en: Journal article reporting three field trials of the Double telepresence robot in two Finnish residential care facilities. It finds the robot increases family presence but raises privacy concerns, especially with mobility, and proposes a draft of ethical guidelines for using telepresence robots in residential care.
annotation.title_clean: Towards Ethical Guidelines of Using Telepresence Robots in Residential Care
annotation.title_en: Towards Ethical Guidelines of Using Telepresence Robots in Residential Care
